feature.title: Sync: dictionary and settings follow you between devices
feature.problem: Every Parley install keeps its own dictionary and settings. A word taught on one Mac, or a gesture key changed there, never reaches the other Mac (or, later, the Android app), so the user teaches the same words twice and the devices drift. The parley-api server (parley-014) now stores both per user. This feature signs the desktop app in to that server with an email, then pushes local edits and pulls remote ones on a timer and soon after any change, last writer wins. A new Sync tab in Settings shows four states: signed out (an email form), signing in, synced (account, last sync time, Sync now), and error (the last failure stays visible). API keys never leave the Mac, and a failed sync never blocks dictation. Frame note: the settings window is not PageShell, so the archetype below is illustrative and not probe-enforced, as in parley-007 to parley-013.
nonGoals: Real identity: sign-in is email to bearer token with no password, good enough for one person on their own server.
Syncing API keys (Groq, Deepgram, MiniMax) or the sync URL, email and switch themselves; those stay on this device.
History and tasks resources: the API has room for them, the desktop does not sync them in v1.
A retry queue or offline journal: a failed run is retried on the next timer tick.
The Android client: it gets its own feature once the API is live.

surfaces.name: Sync tab · signed in
surfaces.purpose: Show that this Mac is signed in, when it last synced, and let the user sync now or sign out.

panels.title: Sync
panels.subtitle: Dictionary and settings follow you. API keys stay here.
rows: Last sync .... 2 min ago   Sync now

states.loading: Signing in: the Sign in button spins and the email field is disabled until the server answers and the first sync finishes. Sync now spins its own button; nothing skeletons.
states.empty: Signed out (no token): the Account group is an email field and a Sign in button. No Sync now, no Last sync row.
states.error: The last run failed: a red Alert titled Last sync failed carries the message ('fetch failed', 'Signed out: the server rejected the token') and the line 'Dictation keeps working; sync retries every five minutes.' A failed sign-in shows its message under the form.
states.success: Synced: the account badge, Last sync as relative time, and after Sync now the outcome line ('Synced 3 up, 1 down'). A gesture key pulled from another device takes effect without a restart.

surfaces.name: Sync tab · signed out
surfaces.purpose: Sign this Mac in to the sync server with an email address.

panels.title: Sync
panels.subtitle: Dictionary and settings follow you. API keys stay here.

states.loading: Sign in pressed: the button shows loading while main asks the server for a token and runs the first sync.
states.empty: The default: sync is off and no token is stored, so only the URL and the email form show.
states.error: An invalid email is refused in the form ('Enter an email address'); a server that cannot be reached or refuses shows its message in a red Alert under the form, and nothing is stored.
states.success: The token is stored encrypted, the switch turns on, and the tab flips to the signed-in layout with 'Signed in and synced'.

components.control: Email TextInput with react-hook-form + zod email, and a Sign in Button with loading
components.why: The same validated-input-plus-action shape AgentUrlSection already uses; the button's loading state is the signing-in state.
components.rejected: A Modal sign-in flow (one field does not earn an overlay), a magic-link step (the API returns the token directly)

components.control: SettingRow + Badge for the account, Switch for Sync, Button for Sync now
components.why: Matches the Agent tab's row language: label left, state and its one action right. The Switch pauses sync without signing out.
components.rejected: A Card per state (heavier than the other tabs), a SegmentedControl for on/off (a binary is a Switch)

components.control: Alert color=red role=alert titled 'Last sync failed'
components.why: The failure persists across reopenings (syncLastError lives in the store), so it is a standing record, not a toast.
components.rejected: Notification toast (gone before the user looks), inline dimmed text (too quiet for a broken sync)
